questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A common law jurisdiction defines first-degree murder as any murder that is (1) committed by means of poison or (2) premeditated. All other murder is second-degree murder, and manslaughter is defined as at common law.
An employee was angry with her boss for denying her a raise. Intending to cause the boss discomfort, the employee secretly dropped into his coffee three over-the-counter laxative pills. The boss drank the coffee containing the pills. Although the pills would not have been dangerous to an ordinary person, because the boss was already taking other medication, he suffered a seizure and died.
If the employee is charged with murder in the first degree, should she be convicted?

choices.A: No.
choices.B: Yes, only because she acted with premeditation.
choices.C: Yes, only because she used poison.
choices.D: Yes, both because she used poison and because she acted with premeditation.

questions.explanation:
Murder is the unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought预怀恶意：普通法谋杀罪的心理要件，包含四种故意/鲁莽心态。 — ie, (1) intent意图：指明知或有意识地追求危害结果发生的心态。 to kill, inflict serious bodily injury, or commit an inherently dangerous felony or (2) reckless disregard鲁莽漠视：明知行为有极高人命风险而仍然不顾后果地去实施。 for a high or obvious risk of death or serious bodily harm (ie, depraved-heart murder极端漠视人命的谋杀（堕落之心谋杀）：对人类生命表现出极端鲁莽漠视而致人死亡。). And in this jurisdiction, murder is elevated to the first degree when the killing is committed with poison毒药：致命或危害健康的化学或生物物质。 or premeditation预谋：在实施犯罪行为前进行了计划、思考或准备。 (ie, planned or reflected upon the killing beforehand).

Here, the employee put laxatives in her boss's coffee after he denied her a raise. When the laxatives mixed with other medication the boss was taking, it killed him. But the employee only intended to cause the boss discomfort — not kill or seriously injure him. And since the laxatives were not dangerous to an ordinary person, there was no high or obvious risk of death or serious bodily harm (no depraved-heart murder). Therefore, the employee did not act with the malice aforethought necessary to be convicted of any degree of murder, including first-degree murder.

(Choices B, C, & D) Premeditation or the use of poison elevates murder from second to first degree in this jurisdiction. But the employee's planning (premeditation) and use of laxatives (a possible poison) are of no consequence here since she lacked the malice aforethought necessary to be convicted of murder in any degree.

📌 Educational Objective

Murder requires proof that the defendant acted with malice aforethought — ie, (1) intent to kill, inflict serious bodily harm, or commit an inherently dangerous felony or (2) reckless disregard for a high or obvious risk of death or serious bodily harm (ie, depraved-heart murder).

如果该员工被控一级谋杀罪，她是否应被定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不应。
zh-choices.B: 是的，仅因为她有预谋行为。
zh-choices.C: 是的，仅因为她使用了毒药。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为她既使用了毒药，又有预谋行为。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法一级谋杀里，预谋（premeditation）或毒药（poison）只是升格条件，前提仍然得先构成谋杀（murder），而本题被告只想让老板不舒服，不到恶意先谋（malice aforethought）。

三秒认题路径：

先看恶意 → 再看谋杀 → 再看一级升格 → 最后排除

核心法律规则

普通法谋杀要求有恶意先谋（malice aforethought），也就是要么有杀人、重伤或实施高度危险重罪的故意（intent），要么对明显的人命风险仍然鲁莽漠视（reckless disregard）。一级谋杀（first-degree murder）只是把已经成立的谋杀再往上分级，所以先问“是不是 murder”，不能倒着只看“像不像 poison / premeditation”。

在这道题里，被告只是想让老板难受，不是想杀人或重伤；而且泻药对普通人也不构成明显致死风险，所以连普通法谋杀都不成立。没有 murder，就没有 first-degree murder 可升级。

核心判例： 无特定判例名称 — 这题锁定的是普通法谋杀的心态门槛：先有 malice aforethought，才谈一级升格。

思维导图

先问：有没有 malice aforethought？
否只想让老板不舒服 → 不是想杀 / 伤
卡死点：没有 murder，就不能进 first-degree
再看有没有明显致死风险？
泻药对普通人不危险 → 不是 depraved-heart murder
最后才看premeditation / poison
这两个只负责“升格”，不能补上缺失的 murder 要件
结论：A，No

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她是偷偷下药，听起来很像poison，而且还是提前想好的，应该直接进一级谋杀。

但考试真正问的是：她有没有先达到murder的心态门槛；没有malice aforethought，再像“预谋”也只是动作像，不会自动变成一级谋杀。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干最关键的事实是她只想让老板难受，且泻药对普通人并不致命，说明没有malice aforethought，所以连 murder 都不成立，更谈不上一级谋杀。

❌ 概念混淆 | 升格前提误判

✕ B: 把premeditation当成独立定罪点了。

❌ 法律适用 | 毒药认定误判

✕ C: 只看poison外观，忽略它没补上 murder 的心态。

❌ 事实误判 | 双重推定偷换

✕ D: 把“像预谋又像投毒”直接偷换成已经构成一级谋杀。

这题建议用什么方法？

先卡住 murder 的心态门槛，再看一级升格条件，别被“下药”这个表面动作带跑。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先有 murder，后谈 first-degree；poison 和 premeditation 只是升格按钮，不是起死回生按钮。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
At a party for coworkers at the manager's home, a salesman accused the manager of making advances toward his wife. The salesman and his wife left the party. The next day at work, the manager saw the salesman and struck him on the head with a glass bottle. The salesman fell into a coma and died two weeks after the incident.
This jurisdiction defines aggravated assault as an assault with any weapon or dangerous implement and punishes it as a felony. It defines murder as the unlawful killing of a person with malice aforethought or in the course of an independent felony.
Under what circumstance may the manager be found guilty of murder?

choices.A: If the jury finds that the killing occurred in the course of an aggravated assault.
choices.B: If the jury finds that the manager intended either to kill or to inflict serious bodily harm.
choices.C: Only if the jury finds that the manager did not act in a rage provoked by the salesman's accusations.
choices.D: Only if the jury finds that the manager intended to kill the salesman.

Intent to kill

Reckless disregard for high risk of death

Killing during

In this jurisdiction, a defendant is guilty of murder if a jury finds beyond a reasonable doubt that he/she unlawfully killed another person (1) with malice aforethought or (2) in the course of an independent felony. Malice aforethought exists when the defendant acts with:

  • intent to kill
  • intent to inflict serious bodily harm (Choice D)
  • reckless disregard of an obvious or high risk to human life (i.e., depraved-heart murder) or
  • intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony (i.e., felony murder).

Here, the manager killed the salesman by striking him on the head with a glass bottle (unlawful killing). Therefore, the manager may be found guilty of murder if the jury also finds that he intended to kill the salesman or to inflict serious bodily harm upon him (malice aforethought).

(Choice A) In this jurisdiction, murder also includes the unlawful killing of another during an independent felony—a felony committed for a purpose other than causing physical harm or death (e.g., burglary). Since aggravated assault requires proof that a dangerous implement was used to inflict (or create imminent apprehension of) harmful contact, it is not an independent felony. Therefore, the manager cannot be found guilty of murder on this basis.

(Choice C) Voluntary manslaughter typically requires proof that a defendant intentionally killed another in an immediate response to adequate provocation—murder does not. Therefore, whether the manager acted in a rage provoked by the salesman's accusations will not affect the manager's potential murder conviction.

📌 Educational Objective

A jury can convict a defendant of murder if it finds beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant unlawfully killed another person with malice aforethought (e.g., intended to kill or inflict serious bodily harm).

该司法管辖区将严重伤害罪（aggravated assault）定义为使用任何武器或危险工具进行的攻击，并将其作为重罪（felony）进行惩罚。该司法管辖区将谋杀罪（murder）定义为怀有预谋恶意（malice aforethought）或在实施一项独立的重罪（independent felony）过程中非法致人死亡的行为。

在何种情况下，该经理可能被判犯有谋杀罪？

zh-choices.A: 如果陪审团认定，该杀人行为发生于实施严重伤害罪（aggravated assault）的过程中。
zh-choices.B: 如果陪审团认定，该经理意图杀人或意图造成严重身体伤害。
zh-choices.C: 只有在陪审团认定该经理的行为并非因销售员的指控所激起的暴怒而为之的情况下。
zh-choices.D: 只有在陪审团认定该经理意图杀害该销售员的情况下。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：谋杀（murder） 的 恶意预谋（malice aforethought），重点看被告是不是有“杀人意图”或“严重伤害意图”。

三秒认题路径：

非法致死 → 看恶意 → 意图杀人/重伤 → 够谋杀 → 选 B

核心法律规则

在这类题里，谋杀（murder） 的核心门槛是 恶意预谋（malice aforethought），考试意思：不是所有打死人都自动降成别的罪，先问有没有“杀人心态”。

恶意预谋（malice aforethought） 包括四种常见形态：意图杀人（intent to kill）、意图造成严重身体伤害（intent to inflict serious bodily injury）、depraved-heart murder，以及 felony murder。

这题最关键的是前两种：只要被告打人时有“想杀”或“至少想造成重伤”的心态，就能进谋杀；不需要真心说出“我要杀死他”这五个字。

核心判例： common law malice aforethought 规则——本题用它锁定“意图杀人或意图重伤”即可成立谋杀。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“非法致死”?
是题干里，经理拿玻璃瓶打头，男销售昏迷两周后死亡，先满足“杀人结果”。
再问：有没有 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）？
有两条最直接：意图杀人（intent to kill） 或 意图造成严重身体伤害（intent to inflict serious bodily injury）。
卡死点：不用去找“独立重罪”或“愤怒辩解”来替代这两个意图。
哪些路会把你带偏？
错路 1aggravated assault 不是本题的 felony murder 入口，因为它本身就是伤害型攻击，不是“独立于致死行为之外”的重罪。
错路 2 “他是不是被刺激到发火”最多碰到 voluntary manslaughter（故意杀人减轻），不能反过来把谋杀门槛抹掉。
结论怎么落？
答案只要陪审团认定他打人时想杀或想造成重伤，就能定谋杀，对应 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是拿玻璃瓶砸人，那是不是要去找“重罪谋杀”或“愤怒杀人”的规则。

但考试真正问的是：这个人当时有没有 恶意预谋（malice aforethought），也就是“想杀”或“想重伤”。司法考试看的是「法律上能不能定罪」，不是「现场看起来有多狠」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 glass bottle 打头 先说明是非法致死；只要再认定他有“想杀”或“想造成严重伤害”的心态，就满足谋杀的 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）。

❌ 事实误判 | 独立重罪误判

✕ A: 把 aggravated assault 当成独立重罪来套重罪谋杀了。

❌ 法律适用 | 减轻事由误判

✕ C: 把事后是否被激怒当成谋杀门槛，混进了 provoked 的思路。

❌ 概念混淆 | 重伤意图漏掉

✕ D: 误以为只有明确说“我要杀”才算数，漏掉了“想造成严重伤害”也够。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓谋杀的心态门槛，再看题干有没有杀人意图或重伤意图，不要被重罪和激情辩解带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：谋杀（murder） 先看 恶意预谋（malice aforethought），其中最常考的就是“想杀”或“想重伤”。

速记口诀：Intent to kill / intent to inflict serious bodily injury 一出现，先往谋杀上想。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man discovered that his business partner was making separate deals with other companies and was filled with rage. The man immediately decided to scare the business partner to force him to stop. The man knew that the business partner went to fitness classes on Wednesday mornings before work, so the following week, the man waited for the business partner to arrive at the gym. Once the man saw the business partner walk inside, the man placed a small bomb under the business partner's car. When the class ended, the man watched as the business partner entered the car and started the engine, causing the bomb to explode and instantly kill him.
A statute in the jurisdiction defines first-degree murder as an intentional and premeditated killing, one occurring during the commission of a common law felony, or one resulting from a heinous act. The statute defines second-degree murder as all other common law murders. Voluntary manslaughter is defined as a killing in the heat of passion upon an adequate legal provocation. Involuntary manslaughter is defined as an unintentional killing committed during an unlawful act or with criminal negligence.
What is the most serious crime for which the man can properly be convicted?

choices.A: First-degree murder.
choices.B: Second-degree murder.
choices.C: Voluntary manslaughter.
choices.D: Involuntary manslaughter.

questions.explanation:
Murder
Common law
  • Unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought:
    • intent to kill
    • intent to cause serious bodily harm
    • depraved-heart murder
    • felony murder
Modern view*
  • First-degree – murder committed due to:
    • premeditation & deliberation
    • heinous act (eg, bombing, torture)
    • enumerated felony
  • Second-degree – any murder that is not first-degree murder
*The fact pattern on the MBE must supply a statute if you are to consider degrees of murder. Otherwise, apply the common-law rule.

Consistent with the modern view, the statute in this jurisdiction defines first-degree murder as:

  • an intentional and premeditated killing
  • a killing committed during the commission of a common law felony or
  • a killing resulting from a heinous act (ie, heinous murder).

A heinous murder is one that results from an especially egregious act, such as ambush (ie, lying in wait), torture, bombing, terrorism, or poisoning. Since the man used a bomb to cause the business partner's death, the man can be convicted of first-degree murder under the statute.

(Choice B) Second-degree murder is defined here as all other common law murders (listed in table above). Since the man only intended to scare the business partner, the man likely committed depraved-heart murder by acting with reckless indifference to human life. However, he can also be convicted of the more serious offense of first-degree murder.

(Choice C) Voluntary manslaughter is defined as a killing that is committed in the heat of passion upon adequate legal provocation.* Discovering that one's business partner is making separate deals is unlikely to constitute adequate provocation. Additionally, there was sufficient time (one week) between the provocation and the killing for a reasonable person to cool off. Therefore, the man would not be convicted of this crime.

*Remember that a killing committed in the heat of passion is not a defense to murder; it merely reduces murder to voluntary manslaughter.

(Choice D) Involuntary manslaughter is defined as an unintentional killing committed during an unlawful act (not seen here) or with criminal negligence—ie, the substantial failure to act as a reasonable person would act under similar circumstances. But the affirmative act of using a bomb goes beyond a mere failure to act.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the modern view, a heinous murder—ie, one that results from an especially egregious act, such as ambush, torture, bombing, terrorism, or poisoning—constitutes first-degree murder.

本题真正考的是：有预谋地用炸弹埋伏杀人，能不能按一级谋杀（first-degree murder）定罪。

三秒认题路径：

埋炸弹 → 蹲守伏击 → 预谋杀人 → 变态/残酷手段 → 一级谋杀

核心法律规则

在现代法下，如果州法把一级谋杀（first-degree murder）定义为“有预谋且故意（premeditated and intentional）”的杀人，或者heinous act（考场意思：特别恶劣的杀法）导致的死亡，就直接进一级。

核心判例： 本题按现代视角的州法规则处理；考试重点是“爆炸/埋伏属于heinous act”，因此可直接锁定一级谋杀。

排除

questions.question:
A state statute divides murder into degrees and defines murder in the first degree as murder committed willfully with premeditation and deliberation. The statute defines murder in the second degree as all other murder at common law and defines voluntary manslaughter as at common law.
A man hated one of his coworkers. Upon learning that the coworker was at a neighbor's house, the man grabbed his gun and went to the neighbor's house hoping to provoke the coworker into attacking him so that he could then shoot the coworker. After arriving at the house, the man insulted the coworker and bragged that he had had sexual relations with the coworker's wife two weeks earlier. This statement was not true, but it enraged the coworker, who grabbed a knife from the kitchen table and ran toward the man. The man then shot and killed the coworker.
What is the most serious homicide offense of which the man could properly be convicted?

choices.A: Murder in the first degree.
choices.B: Murder in the second degree.
choices.C: Voluntary manslaughter, because he provoked the coworker.
choices.D: No form of criminal homicide, because he acted in self-defense.

In this state (and most jurisdictions), the most serious homicide offense is first-degree murder—ie, a killing committed willfully with both:

  • premeditation – when the defendant fully forms the specific intent to kill an appreciable time (no matter how brief) before committing the act and
  • deliberation – when the defendant makes the decision to kill after reflecting on the act and its likely consequences in a cool and dispassionate manner.

Here, the man fully formed the intent to kill his coworker when he grabbed a gun and went to the coworker’s location (premeditation). The man hoped to provoke the coworker into attacking so that he could then shoot the coworker (deliberation). And since the man then willfully shot and killed the coworker, the most serious homicide offense of which the man could be convicted is first-degree murder—unless he has a viable defense.

The man may argue that the coworker’s attack justified the man’s use of deadly force in self-defense. Deadly force is justified when the defendant actually and reasonably believes that such force is necessary to protect himself from imminent death or serious bodily harm. But this defense is generally unavailable if the defendant provoked the victim’s attack—as seen here (Choice D).

(Choice B) In this state, second-degree murder includes all murder at common law—ie, the unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought (eg, intent to kill)—other than first-degree murder. Although the man could be convicted of second-degree murder since he intentionally and unlawfully killed the coworker, he could also be convicted of the more serious crime of first-degree murder.

(Choice C) Voluntary manslaughter is an intentional killing committed (1) in the heat of passion upon adequate provocation or (2) in imperfect self-defense—ie, an honest but unreasonable belief that deadly force is necessary to defend oneself. Here, the man committed the killing after deliberation—not in the heat of passion. And since he purposely provoked the coworker, the man could not honestly act in self-defense.

📌 Educational Objective

First-degree murder encompasses willful killings committed with (1) premeditation—a specific intent to kill fully formed an appreciable time before the killing—and (2) deliberation—a decision to kill made after cool and dispassionate reflection. And though a killing may be justified if the defendant acted in self-defense, this defense is generally unavailable when the defendant was the initial aggressor.

📚 References
  • 40 Am. Jur. 2d Homicide § 43 (2002) (premeditation and deliberation).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告先带枪去找人、故意挑衅对方再开枪杀人，问这还能不能降成 自愿过失杀人（voluntary manslaughter），还是直接算 一级谋杀（first-degree murder）。

三秒认题路径：

先带枪 → 故意挑衅 → 预谋 + 深思 → 不能自卫 → 一级谋杀

核心法律规则

一级谋杀（first-degree murder） 要看两件事：预谋（premeditation），就是先形成杀人故意；深思（deliberation），就是冷静想过再杀。考场意思：不是“临时一气之下”，而是“先想好再动手”。

正当防卫（self-defense） 只有在被告对迫在眉睫的死亡或严重伤害有真实且合理的相信时才成立；但如果是被告先挑衅对方攻击，通常不能拿这条救自己。考场意思：先把人激怒再等他回手，不能把自己包装成无辜防守方。

核心判例： 本题逻辑与 initial aggressor 规则一致：先故意挑衅再杀人，不能靠对方反击洗成防卫。

思维导图

看到“先带枪去找人 + 故意激怒 + 对方持刀冲来”时，先问：这能洗成正当防卫吗？
第 1 关：被告是否先制造冲突？
是：先带枪、再挑衅、等人先动手
第 2 关：有无真实且合理的迫在眉睫危险？
表面有刀冲来，但被告是初始挑衅者
卡死点：初始侵害者（initial aggressor）通常不能主张正当防卫
结论：杀人仍是“故意 + 预谋 + 深思”的一级谋杀
为什么不是降级？ 这里不是“激愤下失手”，而是先去找人、想让对方先打自己，再开枪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：对方真的拿刀冲过来，看起来像 self-defense。

但考试真正问的是：他是不是自己先把局面做成“看起来像防卫”，然后借对方反击开枪。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题里，真正拦住防卫抗辩的不是“有没有危险”，而是“危险是不是被被告自己先做出来的”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 先带枪去找人，又故意挑衅后开枪，说明 预谋（premeditation） 和 深思（deliberation） 都齐了，所以最重只能算一级谋杀。

❌ 概念混淆 | 二级高估误判

✕ B: 只看到“故意杀人”就往二级谋杀套，忘了一级谋杀已经满足。

❌ 法律适用 | 激愤套错位

✕ C: 把 heat of passion 硬塞进来，但他是先算计后动手，不是情绪失控。

❌ 事实误判 | 防卫前提偷换

✕ D: 盯着对方拿刀就忘了他是先挑衅的一方，不能把自己洗成正当防卫。

这题建议用什么方法？

先找“是不是初始侵害者”，再看一级谋杀的预谋和深思是否已经做实。

考场速记

速记口诀：先看有没有 premeditation，再看有没有 deliberation；两项都在，就别被“对方先动手”骗去降级。

questions.question:
A man bought a new rifle and wanted to try it out by doing some target shooting. He went out into the country to an area where he had previously hunted. Much to his surprise, he noticed that the area beyond a clearing contained several newly constructed houses that had not been there before. Between the houses there was a small playground where several children were playing. Nevertheless, the man nailed a paper target to a tree and went to a point where the tree was between himself and the playground. He then fired several shots at the target. One of the shots missed the target and the tree and hit and killed one of the children in the playground.
The man was convicted of murder. He appealed, contending that the evidence was not sufficient to support a conviction of murder.
How should the appellate court rule?

choices.A: Affirm the conviction, as the evidence is sufficient to support a conviction of murder.
choices.B: Reverse the conviction and order the case dismissed, because the evidence is sufficient only for a finding of negligence and negligence alone cannot support a criminal conviction.
choices.C: Reverse the conviction and remand for a new trial, because the evidence is not sufficient for murder but will support a conviction of involuntary manslaughter.
choices.D: Reverse the conviction and remand for a new trial, because the evidence is not sufficient for murder but will support a conviction of voluntary manslaughter.

questions.explanation:
An appellate court should affirm (ie, uphold) a defendant's conviction if a reasonable fact finder could conclude that there was sufficient evidence at trial to establish every element of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt. To support a murder conviction, the evidence must show that the defendant unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—ie, the defendant:

  • intended to kill — acted with purpose or knowledge that his/her actions would cause a death
  • intended to cause serious bodily injury — acted with purpose or knowledge that his/her actions would cause significant but nonfatal injury
  • acted with reckless indifference to an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of serious bodily harm or death (ie, depraved-heart murder) or
  • intended to commit an inherently dangerous felony (ie, felony-murder).

Here, the defendant did not intend to shoot the child, but he knew that several children were playing in a small playground beyond a clearing. Therefore, a reasonable fact finder could conclude that he consciously disregarded the unreasonable risk that he could seriously harm or kill a child by firing several shots in that direction (depraved-heart murder). As a result, there is sufficient evidence to affirm the murder conviction.

(Choice B) Ordinary negligence (ie, the failure to use reasonable care) cannot support a criminal conviction. But here, the evidence is sufficient to support a finding of reckless disregard (ie, malice aforethought) necessary for a murder conviction.

(Choice C) Involuntary manslaughter is an unintentional killing committed (1) with criminal negligence—ie, the substantial failure to exercise reasonable care—or (2) during the commission of an unlawful act—eg, misdemeanor assault. Here, although the man's actions were criminally negligent, they also were serious enough to support his murder conviction.

(Choice D) Voluntary manslaughter is an intentional killing committed in response to adequate provocation or in imperfect self-defense. Since the man acted recklessly (not intentionally) and without provocation or a need for self-defense, the evidence does not support a voluntary manslaughter conviction. But since there is sufficient evidence to support his murder conviction, the court should affirm it.

📌 Educational Objective

Common law murder requires proof that the unlawful killing of another was committed with malice aforethought—eg, proof that the defendant consciously disregarded an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of serious bodily injury or death (depraved-heart murder).

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：明知孩子在射击方向上还连续开枪，是否构成 极端鲁莽杀人（depraved-heart murder），从而足以支持 murder 量刑和维持定罪。

三秒认题路径：

连开枪 → 知有孩子 → 高风险 → 漠视风险 → 维持定罪

核心法律规则

普通法 murder（common law murder） 要求 malice aforethought，考场意思：不是普通粗心，而是对死亡或重伤风险的主观恶性。

其中 depraved-heart murder 的考场意思：行为人明知前方有明显且不合理的致死或重伤高风险，还照做不误；这比 ordinary negligence（普通过失）高得多。

所以这题只要陪审员能合理认定他知道 playground 里有孩子，还朝那个方向连开几枪，murder 就能成立，不必降格成 manslaughter。

核心判例： none needed — 这题直接按 common-law malice 和 depraved-heart 的事实阈值判断。

思维导图

先看：这是不是“故意杀人”式的直接杀人？
否他不是想打孩子，但这不结束分析。
再看：他有没有明知高风险还继续做？
有知道 clearing 后面有 playground，仍然朝那个方向连射。
第三关：风险大不大到足以上升为 malice aforethought？
是这不是一般疏忽，而是对明显致死风险的漠视。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 不是本题；这里的卡死点是“风险被明知却仍放行”。
结论：符合 depraved-heart murder → 选 A，维持 murder 定罪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他不是故意瞄准孩子，只是打靶失手，所以最多算 negligence。

但考试真正问的是：他在明知孩子就在射击方向上时，还连续开枪，是否已经越过“粗心”进入“对生命风险的冷漠放行”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里对应的不是“有没有想杀这个孩子”，而是“明知可能杀人还继续做”，所以会被拉进 murder 而不是简单的 negligence。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 知道 playground 里有孩子 却朝该方向连开几枪，足以让理性裁判认定他对致死风险作出冷漠漠视，构成 depraved-heart murder。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看到失手

✕ B: 把 negligence 当上限，漏掉了他明知有孩子还开枪的更高风险。

❌ 法律适用 | 降格杀人误套

✕ C: 直接跳到 involuntary manslaughter，但题干的风险程度已经够到 murder。

❌ 概念混淆 | 把故意说成冲动

✕ D: voluntary manslaughter 需要挑衅或不完美正当防卫，这里都没有。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓主观恶性层级：普通过失、刑事过失、还是明知高风险仍放行，再决定 murder 还是 manslaughter。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Depraved heart = knew the risk, did it anyway。先问“有没有明知高风险还继续做”，再问“这是不是只是粗心”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
At 11:00 p.m., a husband and wife were accosted in the entrance to their apartment building by a man, who was armed as well as masked. The man ordered the couple to take him into their apartment. After they entered the apartment, the man forced the wife to bind and gag her husband and then to open a safe which contained a diamond necklace. The man then tied her up and fled with the necklace. He was apprehended by apartment building security guards. Before the guards could return to the apartment, but after the man was arrested, the husband, straining to free himself, suffered a massive heart attack and died.
In a common law jurisdiction, which crimes did the man commit?

choices.A: Robbery only.
choices.B: Burglary and robbery only.
choices.C: Robbery and murder only.
choices.D: Burglary, robbery, and murder.

questions.explanation:
Common-law burglary is the (1) breaking and entering of another's dwelling at night (2) with the specific intent to commit a felony therein. The breaking of another's dwelling can be:

  • actual – when physical force is used to gain entry (eg, opening a window) or
  • constructive – when fraud, deception, or threat of force is used to gain entry.

Here, the man ordered the couple to take him into their apartment at gunpoint (constructive breaking). He then entered their apartment at 11:00 at night to rob them (intent to commit felony). Therefore, the man committed burglary (Choices A & C).

Robbery is the use or threat of force to unlawfully take and carry away another's property with the specific intent to permanently deprive the owner of that property. Here, the man used a gun to force the wife to open the safe, took her diamond necklace, and fled. Therefore, he also committed robbery.

After the robbery, the husband died while trying to escape from his binds. Common-law murder, under the felony-murder rule, is any killing of another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony (eg, robbery, burglary). The perpetrator is responsible for deaths that occur after the felony was committed if the death and felony were closely related in time and space (as seen here). Therefore, the man also committed murder (Choices A & B).*

*Under the merger doctrine, the underlying felony will generally merge into felony murder for purposes of the double-jeopardy clause. This means that the defendant cannot be convicted and punished for both the underlying felony and felony murder. However, this question asks which crimes the man committed—not for which crimes the man will ultimately be convicted. Therefore, the merger doctrine is inapplicable.

📌 Educational Objective

Felony murder occurs when the defendant kills another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony—eg, burglary or robbery.

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告先入室抢劫，再在抢劫相关时间空间内导致被害人死亡时，能不能同时认定 burglary（入室盗窃/夜间破门入室）、robbery（抢劫） 和 felony murder（重罪谋杀）。

三秒认题路径：

夜间入室 → 持枪逼迫 → 取走首饰 → 绑缚致死 → 选全都成立

核心法律规则

只抓本题要用的规则

common-law burglary（普通法入室盗窃） 要看夜间进入他人住宅，而且进入时就带着实施重罪的意思；用威胁逼人开门，也算 constructive breaking，考场意思：不是一定要砸门，拿枪逼你放我进去也算“破门”。

robbery（抢劫） 是用暴力或威胁把别人的财物拿走并带走；felony murder（重罪谋杀） 则是人在实施本来就危险的重罪时，顺带造成他人死亡，死亡和重罪在时间、空间上连得很近就够了。

所以这里不是只看“他后来有没有逃掉”，而是看他在入室、抢财物、绑人这一整段里，已经把三项犯罪都做完了。

核心判例： felony-murder rule 逻辑下，抢劫或入室盗窃属于典型的“天然危险重罪”，人在该重罪过程中造成死亡，通常直接触发重罪谋杀。

思维导图

先看：有没有 burglary（入室盗窃）？
YES11:00 p.m. 夜间 + 让夫妻把他带进公寓 = constructive breaking。
卡死点：进屋时就想抢东西，门槛已过。
再看：有没有 robbery（抢劫）？
YES持枪逼妻子绑丈夫、开保险箱、拿走钻石项链并逃走。
最后看：有没有 felony murder（重罪谋杀）？
YES抢劫已发生，丈夫在解绑挣扎时心脏病发死亡，和重罪在时间空间上连得很近。
卡死点：不是看“现场是否继续打人”，而是看死亡是否发生在危险重罪链条里。
结论：Burglary + Robbery + Murder

考点陷阱

你可能会想：人是被抓后才死的，好像就不该算谋杀。

但考试真正问的是：死亡是不是发生在这场 felony murder 链条里，而不是凶手有没有当场亲手继续殴打。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。——本题同理，看的是重罪和死亡有没有在同一犯罪进程里连上。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干先有夜间被迫入室，再有持枪逼迫开保险箱并拿走项链，最后丈夫在挣脱中死亡，三项都被 同一连串事实 一次性满足。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看偷拿

✕ A: 只盯着“拿走项链”robbery，漏掉夜间强行入室和后续死亡。

❌ 事实误判 | 漏掉死亡

✕ B: 把“进屋时就有抢劫意图”当成只有入室，忘了重罪谋杀那条死亡事实。

❌ 法律适用 | 把后死当切断

✕ C: 以为人被抓后才死就断链，但felony murder看的是紧密关联，不是当场持续施暴。

这题建议用什么方法？

按“入室 → 夺财 → 死亡”三段连读，先确认重罪，再用重罪谋杀把死亡接上。

考场速记

记忆口诀：夜入宅、拿财物、死得近，通常就能把 burglary、robbery、felony murder 一起勾出来。

这类题先找“夜间入室”和“危险重罪”，再问死亡有没有跟着这条犯罪链条走。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was at work when he received a call from his wife. She told the man that their neighbor had severely beaten their son for merely walking across the neighbor's lawn. Incensed, the man rushed home from work only to find the neighbor being led away in handcuffs by the police. Ten days later, the man was shopping at a local grocery store when he spotted the neighbor, who had been released on bail. As they crossed paths, the neighbor looked directly at the man and said, "Hitting your boy sure was fun." The man became enraged, immediately drew a knife, and stabbed the neighbor repeatedly, killing him.
The man was charged with murder. At trial, the man has requested that the court instruct the jury on voluntary manslaughter.
Should the court grant the man's request?

choices.A: No, because a reasonable person in the man's position would have cooled after 10 days.
choices.B: No, because words alone do not constitute adequate provocation.
choices.C: Yes, because the man had not actually cooled off in the days between the son's beating and the neighbor's death.
choices.D: Yes, because the neighbor's taunt provoked the man again.

questions.explanation:
Rekindling doctrine

A court should issue an instruction on any offense of which a reasonable jury could convict the defendant. In a prosecution for murder, an instruction on voluntary manslaughter is warranted when a reasonable jury could find that the defendant intentionally killed the victim:

  • in response to adequate provocation – an act that would cause a sudden and intense passion in a reasonable person (eg, serious assault on a family member) and
  • in the heat of passion – a reasonable person would not have cooled off in the time between the provocation and the killing, and the defendant did not cool off.

However, the rekindling doctrine allows a defendant to argue that, even though enough time had passed since the initial provocation to allow for cooling off, another encounter with the victim was sufficient to "rekindle" the defendant's passion. Such encounters commonly involve mocking or taunts about the initial provocation.

Here, the man was adequately provoked after the neighbor severely beat the man's son. However, a reasonable person likely would have cooled off in the 10 days between the son's beating and the man's encounter with the neighbor. But since a reasonable jury could find that the neighbor's taunt—"Hitting your boy sure was fun"—was sufficient to rekindle the man's passion, the court should grant his request for a voluntary-manslaughter instruction (Choice D).

(Choice B) Mere words are typically not enough to constitute adequate provocation. But a second encounter involving taunting or mocking may be sufficient to rekindle passion from a prior adequate provocation (as seen here).

(Choice C) The man may not have actually cooled off in the time between the son's beating and the man's encounter with the neighbor. But since a reasonable person likely would have, this does not provide a basis for an instruction on voluntary manslaughter.

📌 Educational Objective

Voluntary manslaughter is an intentional killing committed (1) in response to adequate provocation and (2) in the heat of passion. But even if enough time had passed for cooling off, a secondary encounter with the victim may be sufficient to rekindle the defendant's passion under the rekindling doctrine.

📚 References
  • People v. Berry, 556 P.2d 777 (Cal. 1976) (establishing the rekindling doctrine).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：自发热情谋杀减轻为自愿过失杀人（voluntary manslaughter）时，前一次足够的挑衅即使已经过了冷静期，也可能被后来的嘲讽“重新点燃”。

三秒认题路径：

故意杀人 → 挑衅先在前 → 10天已冷静 → 讽刺再点火 → 可要减责

核心法律规则

自愿过失杀人（voluntary manslaughter）要求：故意杀人是出于adequate provocation，并且发生在heat of passion里。考场意思：不是在冷静后慢慢报复，而是被刺激后立刻失控出手。

一般来说，若理性人已经有时间冷静，减责就断了；但rekindling doctrine（重新点燃原则）允许你说：前面的刺激虽然过了时间，后来又见到对方并被嘲讽，激情被重新点燃了。考场意思：后来的话不是“普通闲聊”，而是把前面的怒火重新拉回现场。

核心判例： People v. Berry — 认可“重新点燃”逻辑：后续挑衅可让原本已过冷静期的激情再次成立。

思维导图

先问：这是不是还能给voluntary manslaughter指示？
1. 有无前置足够挑衅？
邻居严重殴打儿子 → 这是足够挑衅
2. 冷静期是否已过？
10天后在超市相遇 → 理性人通常已冷静
3. 但有没有二次“点火”？
邻居说“Hitting your boy sure was fun”
嘲讽式重提旧伤 → 重新点燃激情
结论：
理性陪审团可认定仍在热情中 → 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：mere words 一般不算充分挑衅，所以 B 说得对。

但考试真正问的是：这里不是单看“话语本身”，而是看它是否把前面的充分挑衅重新点燃。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干先有儿子被严重殴打这一足够挑衅，后有邻居当面嘲讽，足以让合理陪审团认定激情被重新点燃，所以可给自愿过失杀人指示。

❌ 事实误判 | 冷静期过读

✕ A: 只盯着10 days，漏掉后来的重新点火。

❌ 概念混淆 | 纯言辞误判

✕ B: 把后来的嘲讽当成单独考点，忘了它是在“复燃”旧怒火。

❌ 法律适用 | 冷静标准错位

✕ C: 只看他自己还没冷静，忽略理性人早已能冷静下来。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“前置足够挑衅+后来再点火”，再判断冷静期是否被重新打断。

考场速记

记住这句：先有足够挑衅，后有重新点火，就能把 voluntary manslaughter 从“已冷静的报复”里捞出来。

questions.question:
A man purchased a new rifle and wanted to try it out before bringing it on a hunting trip the following day. After leaving the gun store, the man drove to a remote part of town and stopped at a building that, by all outward appearances, had been abandoned. The man fired upon the building, using the building's boarded-up windows as targets. Unbeknownst to the man, a small group of people had taken shelter inside the building. The man ceased firing once he heard voices yelling from inside the building. However, one of the man's bullets struck and killed a woman inside the building.
The above facts were set out at trial, and the man was convicted of murder. On appeal, the man argues that the evidence was insufficient to support his conviction.
If the jurisdiction follows the common law of homicide, should the man's conviction be overturned?

choices.A: No, because the killing occurred during the commission of an inherently dangerous felony.
choices.B: No, because the man acted with negligent disregard of an obviously high risk of death by shooting at the building.
choices.C: Yes, because the man did not intend to kill the woman when he fired at the building.
choices.D: Yes, because the man was unaware of the danger posed by firing at the seemingly abandoned building.

questions.explanation:
Homicide
Common law Modern approach
Murder Unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought:
  • Intent to kill
  • Intent to cause serious bodily harm
  • Depraved-heart murder
  • Felony murder
 First-degree: murder committed with:
  • premeditation & deliberation
  • heinous acts (eg, bombing, torture)
  • enumerated felony murder
Second-degree: any murder that is not first-degree murder
Voluntary
manslaughter		 Intentional killing mitigated by either:
  • adequate provocation (ie, heat of passion)
  • other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
Involuntary
manslaughter		 Unintentional killing either:
  • caused by criminal negligence (or recklessness under MPC)
  • occurs during commission of criminal act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter)
MPC = Model Penal Code.

A conviction should be overturned if the evidence was insufficient to support a guilty verdict because no reasonable fact finder could find proof of every element of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt. Common-law murder requires proof that the defendant unlawfully killed another while acting with malice aforethought—ie:

  • intent to kill
  • intent to inflict serious bodily injury
  • reckless disregard of an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of causing death or serious bodily injury (ie, depraved-heart murder) or
  • intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony (ie, felony-murder rule)

Here, the man did not intend to kill or seriously injure the woman, and firing a rifle at a seemingly abandoned building does not qualify as an inherently dangerous felony (Choices A & C). However, he could still be guilty of depraved-heart murder if he recklessly disregarded an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of causing death or serious bodily injury by shooting at the building.

In a majority of jurisdictions (and under the Model Penal Code), a defendant must have actually realized the danger to human life or safety posed by his/her conduct to be guilty of depraved-heart murder.* Here, there is no evidence that the man was actually aware of the danger posed by his conduct because the building was in a remote area and lacked signs of being occupied. Therefore, his conviction should be overturned.

*A minority of jurisdictions impose guilt for depraved-heart murder if a reasonable person in the defendant's position would have realized the danger posed by his/her conduct.

(Choice B) Involuntary manslaughter requires proof that the defendant unintentionally killed another with criminal negligence or during the commission of an unlawful act. But since the man was convicted of murder, not involuntary manslaughter, the fact that he may have been negligent is irrelevant to his appeal.

📌 Educational Objective

Depraved-heart murder is the reckless disregard of an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of causing death or serious bodily injury. In most jurisdictions, the defendant must actually realize the danger posed by his/her conduct to be convicted of common-law murder under this standard.

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Unintended killings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非预谋恶意杀人（depraved-heart murder） 需看被告是否实际意识到对人命的高风险；如果只是事后看来“很危险”，但当时并不知道有人在里面，常常达不到谋杀。

三秒认题路径：

未预见人 → 危险射击 → 看恶意 → 看实际意识 → 不能定罪

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

普通法谋杀（common law murder） 要有 malice aforethought，常见来源包括：故意杀人、故意重伤、非预谋恶意（depraved-heart murder）、或 felony murder。这里真正卡点是第三种：必须是对明显且不合理高风险的 reckless disregard，考场意思：不是“现在看起来很冒险”就够了，而是被告当时得真的知道自己在把人命往火坑里推。
在多数法域和 Model Penal Code（MPC） 下，得证明被告实际意识到该危险；如果题干只显示他以为建筑废弃、看不出有人在内，就很难证明这种恶意。

核心判例： depraved-heart murder 的多数法域标准要求主观上实际意识到危险；本题因缺少这种意识，不能靠“事后觉得危险”补成谋杀。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 普通法谋杀（common law murder） 的 malice aforethought 问题？
NO不成立故意杀人，也不是故意重伤。
YES继续看 非预谋恶意（depraved-heart murder）。
第二关：被告当时有没有真的知道，自己在制造“对人命的明显高风险”？
看见有人还继续射击 → 更像恶意。
没看出有人只是在远处打“看似废弃”的楼 → 主观恶意断掉。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 这类概念不在本题；本题要的是“当时是否知道危险”。
结论：证据最多支持“粗心/疏忽”，但不够支撑谋杀 → 选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他朝“建筑”开枪，结果死人了，看起来很危险，所以一定是谋杀。

但考试真正问的是：他在开枪时有没有意识到楼里有人，是否真的在对人命作 reckless disregard。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。（本题对应的思路就是：不是“结果很惨”就自动升级为谋杀。）

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最关键的 remote area 和 seemingly abandoned 说明他并不知道楼里有人，少了“实际意识到高风险”这一步，普通法下就难认 depraved-heart murder。

❌ 法律适用 | 内含重罪误套

✕ A: 把 inherently dangerous felony 硬套上去，但朝废楼试枪不是这个重罪谋杀场景。

❌ 概念混淆 | 过失等级错位

✕ B: 用 negligent disregard 偷换成“过失就够”，可本题审的是更高的谋杀恶意。

❌ 事实误判 | 只盯无意结果

✕ C: 只抓 did not intend，却忘了非预谋恶意不要求故意杀人。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看被告当时知不知道屋里有人，再判断是“疏忽”还是“恶意”。

考场速记

记住这句：depraved-heart murder 不是“结果吓人”，而是“当时明知有致命高风险还照做”。本题的快捷口诀就是：先找主观意识，再看危险程度，最后才谈谋杀。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Despondent over losing his job, a man drank all night at a bar. While driving home, he noticed a car following him and, in his intoxicated state, concluded he was being followed by robbers. In fact, a police car was following him on suspicion of drunk driving. In his effort to get away, the man sped through a stop sign and struck and killed a pedestrian. He was arrested by the police.
The man is prosecuted for manslaughter. What verdict should the jury render?

choices.A: Acquittal, because he honestly believed he faced an imminent threat of death or severe bodily injury.
choices.B: Acquittal, because his intoxication prevented him from appreciating the risk he created.
choices.C: Conviction, because he acted recklessly and his apprehension of danger was not reasonable.
choices.D: Conviction, because he acted recklessly and in fact was in no danger.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of mistake-of-fact defense

Type of mens rea
Strict liability crime (eg, statutory rape)
Specific intent (eg, first-degree murder)
General intent & malice (eg, involuntary manslaughter)
Never a defense
Honest mistake
negates specific
intent
Honest & reasonable
mistake negates
mens rea

In most jurisdictions, manslaughter is divided into two types:

  • Voluntary manslaughter – an intentional killing mitigated by adequate provocation (ie, heat of passion) or other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
  • Involuntary manslaughter – an unintentional killing committed during an unlawful act or with criminal negligence—the substantial failure to act as a reasonable person would act under similar circumstances (sometimes called recklessness)

Mistake of fact is a defense to manslaughter (and other general intent crimes) when the defendant's honest, reasonable, but mistaken belief negates the requisite mental state (ie, mens rea).

Here, the man sped through a stop sign and unintentionally killed a pedestrian. He acted recklessly (ie, with criminal negligence) since a reasonable person would not have driven while intoxicated and run a stop sign. And though he honestly believed that robbers were pursuing him and that he needed to escape this threat of harm, his mistaken belief was unreasonable since it was brought about by his intoxication—not his pursuers (the police). Therefore, the jury should convict the man of involuntary manslaughter (Choice A).

(Choice B) Voluntary intoxication is a defense to specific intent crimes when it prevents the defendant from forming the requisite intent. But it is not a defense to crimes requiring a lesser mens rea (eg, involuntary manslaughter). So though the man's voluntary intoxication may have prevented him from appreciating the risk he created, it is no defense here.

(Choice D) Although the man acted recklessly and was not actually in danger, his honest but mistaken belief that he was in danger could have been a defense had that belief been reasonable.

📌 Educational Objective

Mistake of fact is a defense to non-specific intent crimes (eg, manslaughter) when the defendant's honest, reasonable, but mistaken belief negates the requisite mental state.

一名男子因失业而心灰意冷，在酒吧整夜饮酒。在开车回家的路上，他注意到一辆车在跟踪他，并在醉酒状态下断定自己被劫匪跟踪。事实上，是一辆警车因怀疑他酒后驾驶而跟踪他。为了逃跑，该男子超速闯过一个停车标志，撞死了一名行人。他被警方逮捕。

该男子被以过失杀人罪（manslaughter）起诉。陪审团应作出何种裁决？

zh-choices.A: 无罪，因为他真诚地相信自己面临着死亡或严重身体伤害的即时威胁。
zh-choices.B: 无罪，因为他的醉酒状态使他无法意识到自己所造成的风险。
zh-choices.C: 有罪，因为他的行为鲁莽，并且他对危险的恐惧是不合理的。
zh-choices.D: 有罪，因为他的行为鲁莽，且事实上他并未处于危险之中。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Mens Rea- State of Mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：过失杀人（manslaughter）里，误认事实（mistake of fact）只有在“真诚且合理”时才可能帮你挡掉所需的 mens rea，而这题里的恐惧是被酒精放大的，不够合理。

三秒认题路径：

酒后驾车 → 误认追车 → 闯停牌 → 过失致死 → 不能免责

核心法律规则

非故意杀人（involuntary manslaughter）看的是 recklessness 或 criminal negligence，考场意思：你是不是把“普通人会避开的风险”硬撞上去了。

误认事实（mistake of fact）只有在“真诚而且合理”时，才可能打掉一般故意罪或此类低阶 mens rea；如果错误是醉酒自己放大的，就不算合理。

所以这题不看他主观上怕不怕，而看他在醉酒状态下闯停牌、撞死行人的行为，已经满足了过失杀人的心态门槛。

核心判例： 这里的规则与传统 MBE 立场一致：honest and reasonable mistake 才能帮忙；本题的错误判断不合理，所以仍定罪。

思维导图

先看：他是不是只是“真怕”就能无罪？
1. 先定罪名：manslaughter，不是需要特殊意图的罪。
2. 再看抗辩：mistake of fact 只能救“真诚且合理”的错误。
3. 本题卡点：他是醉酒后把警车看成劫匪车，错误来源不合理。
卡死点：reasonable 没过，所以不能把 recklessness 洗掉。
4. 结果：仍属 involuntary manslaughter，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他主观上真的以为自己在躲抢劫，应该算正当。

但考试真正问的是：这个误认合不合理，以及它能不能真的挡掉 manslaughter 需要的危险驾驶心态。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里他喝醉后闯停牌、撞死行人，已经是 recklessly；他把警车看成劫匪车的判断又不合理，所以仍构成过失杀人。

❌ 概念混淆 | 正当化误判

✕ A: 把“我真害怕”当成免责，混成自卫了。

❌ 事实误判 | 酒精借口放大

✕ B: 盯着 intoxication 就想放人，但这不是特定意图罪。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看无险事实

✕ D: 只说“其实没危险”不够，关键是他仍然把危险跑出来了。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man became ill while at work and decided to go home early. When he entered his bedroom, the man saw his wife engaged in sexual intercourse with a neighbor. The man grabbed a gun from a dresser drawer and shot and killed the neighbor. He was later charged and prosecuted.
In a jurisdiction that follows the common law for homicide offenses, which crimes should the court instruct the jury on?

choices.A: Murder and involuntary manslaughter.
choices.B: Murder and voluntary manslaughter.
choices.C: Murder, voluntary manslaughter, and involuntary manslaughter.
choices.D: Voluntary manslaughter and involuntary manslaughter.

questions.explanation:
Types of common-law homicide
(in descending order of seriousness)
Murder Unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought:
  • Intent to kill
  • Intent to cause serious physical injury
  • Depraved heart – reckless disregard of obvious/unjustifiably high risk to human life
  • Felony murder – intent to commit inherently dangerous felony
Voluntary
manslaughter		 Intentional killing of another based on:
  • adequate provocation or
  • imperfect self-defense:
    • defendant started confrontation
    • defendant honestly but unreasonably believed deadly force was necessary
Involuntary
manslaughter		 Unintentional killing of another:
  • with criminal negligence or
  • during unlawful act

A court should instruct the jury on all possible crimes for which a reasonable fact finder could convict a defendant. Therefore, an instruction on common law murder is appropriate when a reasonable jury could conclude that the defendant unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—e.g., the defendant acted with the specific intent to kill or inflict serious bodily harm upon the victim.

Here, the man shot and killed the neighbor (unlawful killing). A reasonable jury could find that the man acted with malice aforethought since he grabbed a gun from a dresser drawer and shot the neighbor after finding him engaged in sexual intercourse with the man's wife (intent to kill or seriously harm). Therefore, the court should instruct the jury on murder.

Additionally, an instruction on voluntary manslaughter (i.e., heat-of-passion killing) is appropriate when a reasonable jury could find that the defendant intentionally killed another in response to adequate provocation. Provocation is adequate if it would cause a reasonable person to lose control—e.g., discovering one's spouse engaged in adultery (as seen here). Therefore, the court should also instruct the jury on voluntary manslaughter.

(Choices A, C & D) Involuntary manslaughter is an unintentional killing caused by an unlawful act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter) or criminal negligence (i.e., the substantial failure to act as a reasonably prudent person). Here, since the evidence shows that the man intended to kill or seriously harm his neighbor, a jury instruction on involuntary manslaughter is inappropriate.

📌 Educational Objective

A jury instruction on common law murder is appropriate when a reasonable fact finder could conclude that the defendant unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought (e.g., intended to kill or inflict serious bodily harm). And a voluntary manslaughter instruction is appropriate if the jury could find adequate provocation for the killing.

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：看到配偶通奸后当场开枪杀人，法院要不要同时讲 murder（谋杀） 和 voluntary manslaughter（自愿过失杀人），而不是把它当成不小心杀人。

三秒认题路径：

当场撞见通奸 → 立刻开枪 → 有杀意 → 可能是谋杀 → 也可能是激愤杀人

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

murder（谋杀） 要看有没有 malice aforethought（预谋恶意）；只要证据足以让合理陪审团认为被告是想杀人，或想造成严重人身伤害，就要讲这一项。

voluntary manslaughter（自愿过失杀人） 是“有意杀人，但因为 adequate provocation（充分挑衅） 一时失控”。看到自己配偶正在通奸，通常就是 MBE 里最经典的充分挑衅。

involuntary manslaughter（非自愿过失杀人） 讲的是“无意致死”，靠的是刑事过失或违法行为；题干既然已经写明他拿枪射杀，就不是这个方向。

核心判例： 无。这题考的是普通法杀人分层规则：有杀意就看 murder，有充分挑衅就再看 voluntary manslaughter。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 无意致死？
不是。 题干写的是“拿枪射杀邻居”，先锁定 intent to kill（故意杀人） 或至少 intent to cause serious bodily harm（故意重伤）。
再问：有没有 malice aforethought（预谋恶意）？
有。 看到配偶通奸后立刻开枪，合理陪审团可以认定是有意杀人，所以先进入 Murder。
再问：有没有把 murder 拉低成 voluntary manslaughter 的 adequate provocation（充分挑衅）？
有。 当场撞见配偶通奸，是普通法里最典型的激愤场景，所以不能卡死在“只有 murder”，陪审团也应被告知 Voluntary manslaughter。
最后排除：involuntary manslaughter。
排除。 这不是“不小心杀人”，而是“有意开枪”，所以 非自愿过失杀人不讲。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是看到配偶出轨才动手，好像应该只算“情绪激动”，所以可以直接跳到自愿过失杀人。

但考试真正问的是：陪审团要不要同时听到 murder 和 voluntary manslaughter 两个层级；只要事实足以支持有意杀人，就不能把 murder 关掉。

司法考试看的是「法律上能不能同时成立哪个罪名」，而不是「故事里谁更可怜」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 拿枪当场射杀邻居 足以支持 murder（谋杀）；同时 撞见配偶通奸 又给了 adequate provocation（充分挑衅），所以还要讲 voluntary manslaughter（自愿过失杀人）。

❌ 事实误判 | 误读无意致死

✕ A: 把 involuntary 当成“情绪冲动”了；题干明写他是开枪故意杀人。

❌ 概念混淆 | 过度并列全选

✕ C: 想把所有层级都塞进去，但 involuntary manslaughter 被事实直接排掉了。

❌ 法律适用 | 误把挑衅当唯一答案

✕ D: 只盯着通奸挑衅，却忘了题干也支持 murder。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“故意杀人”还是“无意致死”，再看有没有充分挑衅把谋杀降格。

考场速记

记住这个顺序：先看 murder，再看 voluntary manslaughter，最后才排 involuntary manslaughter。撞见配偶通奸是经典 adequate provocation（充分挑衅），但只要题干还是“故意开枪”，谋杀层级也不能漏掉。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man decided to kill his boss after she told him that he would be fired if his work did not improve. The man knew his boss was scheduled to go on a business trip on Monday morning. On Sunday morning, the man went to the company parking garage and put a bomb in the company car that his boss usually drove. The bomb was wired to go off when the car engine started. The man then left town. At 5:00 a.m. Monday, the man, after driving all night, was overcome with remorse and had a change of heart. He called the security officer on duty at the company and told him about the bomb. The security officer said he would take care of the matter. An hour later, the officer put a note on the boss's desk telling her of the man's call. The officer then looked at the car but could not see any signs of a bomb. He printed a sign saying, "DO NOT USE THIS CAR," put it on the windshield, and went to call the police. Before the police arrived, the company's vice president got into the car and started the engine. The bomb went off, killing her instantly.
The jurisdiction defines murder in the first degree as any homicide committed with premeditation and deliberation or any murder in the commission of a common law felony. Second-degree murder is defined as all other murder at common law. Manslaughter is defined by the common law.
What is the most serious crime of which the man can be properly convicted?

choices.A: Murder in the first degree, because, with premeditation and deliberation, he killed whoever would start the car.
choices.B: Murder in the second degree, because he had no intention of killing the company vice president.
choices.C: Manslaughter, because he had no intent to kill at the time of the explosion.
choices.D: Only attempted murder of his boss, because the vice president's death was the result of the security officer's negligence.

questions.explanation:
In this jurisdiction, first-degree murder includes felony murder and any homicide that is committed with:

  • premeditation – the defendant formed the specific intent to kill at some appreciable time before committing the criminal act and
  • deliberation – the defendant reached the decision to kill after cool and dispassionate reflection upon the criminal act and its likely consequences.

And under the doctrine of transferred intent, the defendant's specific intent to kill one person will be transferred to the person actually harmed by the defendant.

Here, the man planned to kill his boss (premeditation and deliberation) and planted a bomb in her car to do so. The bomb then killed the vice president. And though the man did not intend to kill the vice president, his intent to kill his boss with the bomb can be shifted onto the vice president under the doctrine of transferred intent (Choice B). Therefore, the man can be convicted of first-degree murder.

(Choice C) All crimes require proof of concurrence—ie, that the defendant had the requisite intent when the criminal act was committed. Here, the man had no intent to kill at the time of the explosion. But he did act with such intent when he committed the criminal act of planting the car bomb. And since that bomb caused the vice president's death, the man can be convicted of first-degree murder.

(Choice D) Although the man is guilty of attempted murder of his boss, he is also guilty of first-degree murder of the vice president. The security officer's negligence did not absolve the man of murder because the officer's actions were foreseeable—ie, not a superseding cause that would eliminate the man's liability.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the doctrine of transferred intent, the defendant's specific intent to kill one person will be transferred to the person actually harmed by the defendant.

该司法管辖区将一级谋杀罪(murder in the first degree)定义为任何有预谋和深思熟虑的杀人行为，或在实施普通法重罪过程中发生的任何谋杀。二级谋杀罪(second-degree murder)被定义为普通法上的所有其他谋杀。非预谋杀人罪(Manslaughter)由普通法定义。

该男子可被适当定罪的最严重罪行是什么？

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Mens Rea- State of Mind

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告先带着杀老板的故意埋炸弹，后来受害人换成了副总裁时，转移故意（transferred intent）能不能把这个故意“转”过去，成立一级谋杀。

三秒认题路径：

先有杀意 → 先设炸弹 → 死的是别人 → 转移故意 → 一级谋杀

核心法律规则

一级谋杀（first-degree murder）考场意思：这里最核心的是预谋（premeditation）和深思熟虑（deliberation），不是看最后死的人是不是他原本点名要杀的那个人。

转移故意（transferred intent）考场意思：如果他本来就有杀人故意，只是打到的是“旁人”，这份故意会跟着结果走，所以杀错人也还是按故意杀人算。

因果关系（causation）考场意思：中间那位保安没有形成真正的介入致因（superseding cause），所以不会把他的杀人责任切断。

核心判例：Transferred intent 的经典思路就是：杀老板的故意可以转到实际被炸死的人身上，所以仍可定一级谋杀。

思维导图

先问：这是“故意杀错人”还是“只是没想到会死到别人身上”？
事实起点先想杀老板，已经把炸弹装进公司车里。
法律关卡有预谋（premeditation） + 深思熟虑（deliberation），故意不是临时起意。
转移规则真正被炸死的是副总裁，但故意会转移故意（transferred intent）到实际受害人。
卡死点：不是“他原本想杀谁”，而是“他有没有带着杀人故意做出致死行为”。
结论故意杀人仍成立，而且是一级谋杀，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他最后没想杀副总裁，而且开枪/爆炸时人已经改了主意，所以只能算较轻的罪。

但考试真正问的是：他在放置炸弹那一刻已经形成杀人故意，后面“后悔了”不等于把已经启动的致死行为洗掉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里他先对老板形成杀人故意并埋下炸弹，实际死者虽是副总裁，但转移故意（transferred intent）仍让一级谋杀成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 只看死者姓名

✕ B: 把“没想杀副总裁”当成免责点，忽略故意会跟着结果走。

❌ 法律适用 | 把撤回当无罪

✕ C: 误以为他后来had a change of heart，就能抹掉前面的故意。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大他人过失

✕ D: 把保安的处理说成切断因果，但这点不足以变成介入致因。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“先有故意再发生结果”这条链，再看转移故意和因果是否被切断。

考场速记

记住一句：先有杀意，后死他人，就先想转移故意（transferred intent）；只要没有真正的介入致因，还是按故意杀人处理。

questions.question:
A man and his friend were watching a televised football game at the man's home. Upset by a penalty called by the referee, the friend threw a bottle of beer at the man's television, breaking the screen. Enraged, the man picked up a nearby hammer and hit the friend on the head with it. The friend died from the blow.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness.
In a jurisdiction that follows common law principles, what is the most serious crime of which the man could properly be convicted?

choices.A: Murder.
choices.B: Voluntary manslaughter.
choices.C: Involuntary manslaughter.
choices.D: Assault.

questions.explanation:
Common law murder

Did defendant cause another’s death?
  • Actual cause: but for or substantial factor
AND
  • Proximate cause: death was foreseeable
No → Not guilty
Yes ↓
Did defendant act with malice aforethought?
  • Reckless disregard of obvious/high risk
    of death or serious bodily harm
  • Intent to commit Inherently
    dangerous felony
  • Intent to cause Serious physical injury
  • Intent to Kill
Mnemonic: RISK
No → Not guilty
Yes ↓
Guilty

Under the common law, a defendant can be convicted of murder if he/she unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—ie, acted with:

  • intent to kill – the purpose or knowledge to a substantial certainty that death will result
  • intent to inflict serious physical harm
  • reckless disregard for an obvious or unjustifiably high risk to human life or
  • intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony.

Here, the man killed his friend by hitting the friend on the head with a hammer. And a reasonable jury could find that the man acted with malice aforethought—(1) the intent to kill or seriously injure his friend with the hammer or (2) a reckless disregard of the obvious risk that his conduct would kill his friend. Therefore, the most serious crime of which the man could be convicted is murder.

(Choice B) Voluntary manslaughter is the intentional killing of another in response to adequate provocation—ie, conduct or circumstances that would cause a reasonable person to lose control. But since a reasonable person would not hit someone on the head with a hammer in response to a broken television screen (no adequate provocation), the man will likely not be convicted of this crime.

(Choice C) Involuntary manslaughter is the unintentional killing of another without malice aforethought through criminal negligence or an unlawful act. But here, a reasonable jury could find that the man acted with malice aforethought, so he could be convicted of the more serious crime of murder.

(Choice D) Assault occurs when a defendant (1) attempts to commit a battery or (2) intentionally places a victim in fear of imminent harmful contact. Although the man may have committed assault, the most serious crime of which he could be convicted is murder.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant is guilty of common law murder when a jury finds that he/she unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—eg, intent to kill or inflict serious bodily harm, reckless disregard for an obvious or unjustifiably high risk to human life.

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：普通法 谋杀（murder） 是否成立，关键看“杀人结果 + 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）”，不是看被激怒后就自动降成过失杀人。

三秒认题路径：

打头致死 → 先看杀人结果 → 再看 malice → 无充分挑衅 → 选 Murder

核心法律规则

普通法谋杀（common law murder） 要先看是否造成他人死亡，再看有没有 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）。这里的 malice 不只等于“想杀”，也包括明知会造成严重身体伤害还去做，或对明显且不合理的死亡风险漠视。自愿过失杀人（voluntary manslaughter） 需要 充分挑衅（adequate provocation），而不是单纯生气。非自愿过失杀人（involuntary manslaughter） 是没有 malice 的非故意致死；一旦 jury 能看出 malice，题目就往 murder 走。

核心判例： 这题不靠特定判例转弯，直接套 common law murder 的 malice 规则；看见致死再接 hammer 这类明显危险行为，优先想到 murder。

思维导图

先问：被告是否造成他人死亡？
是：看实际因果关系（but for / substantial factor）+ 可预见近因；本题已被锤击致死，先过这一关。
再问：是否有 恶意预谋（malice aforethought）？
四个入口：intent to kill、intent to inflict serious physical harm、reckless disregard、inherently dangerous felony。
卡死点：朋友只是砸电视，不是会让理性人失控的充分挑衅，所以不能靠 voluntary manslaughter 逃掉。
hammer 打头 = 明知会造成重伤/死亡的风险，足够支撑 malice。
否：才会往无罪或较轻罪名看；但本题事实已经把 malice 推出来了。
结论：最重可定 Murder。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是被气到才动手，应该往 voluntary manslaughter 想。

但考试真正问的是：有没有 充分挑衅（adequate provocation），不是有没有“很生气”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

朋友打坏电视只是在惹人生气，不是足以让理性人失控的法律挑衅；拿锤子砸头，反而把题目推回 murder。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里他用锤子击打头部并导致死亡，足以看出 malice aforethought，所以最重可定 Murder。

❌ 概念混淆 | 挑衅门槛误判

✕ B: 把 adequate provocation 想太低了，砸坏电视还不够。

❌ 法律适用 | 轻罪层级误判

✕ C: 误把有恶意的致死当成无恶意致死了。

❌ 事实误判 | 动作结果偷换

✕ D: assault 只是前置动作，题目已经问到致死后的最重罪名。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否致死”，再看 malice；只要没有充分挑衅，就不要被 voluntary manslaughter 牵走。

考场速记

记住一条：murder = death + malice aforethought；看到锤子打头、明显危险、没有充分挑衅，先往 murder 选。

口诀可记成 RISK：Reckless disregard、Intent to kill、Serious bodily harm、Killing via dangerous felony。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man joined a neighborhood gang. At a gang meeting, as part of the initiation process, the leader ordered the man to kill a member of a rival gang. The man refused, saying he no longer wanted to be part of the group. The leader, with the approval of the other members, told the man that he had become too involved with the gang to quit and that they would kill him if he did not accomplish the murder of the rival gang member. The next day the man shot the rival gang member to death while he was sitting on his motorcycle outside a restaurant.
The man is charged with first-degree murder. First-degree murder is defined in the jurisdiction as the intentional premeditated killing of another. Second-degree murder is all other murder at common law.
If the man killed the rival gang member because of the threat to his own life, what verdict should the jury render?

choices.A: Guilty of first-degree murder.
choices.B: Guilty of second-degree murder.
choices.C: Not guilty, because of the defense of duress.
choices.D: Not guilty, because of the defense of necessity.

questions.explanation:
Duress v. Necessity
Duress
  • Crime (other than murder) committed under imminent unlawful threat of serious bodily harm from human force
  • Reasonable belief that crime was necessary to prevent harm to self or others
  • No reasonable opportunity to escape
Necessity
  • Crime (other than murder) committed to prevent imminent & substantial harm from natural* or human force
  • No reasonable legal alternative available
  • Harm caused < harm avoided
*At common law, necessity had to arise from natural forces. But many jurisdictions have now expanded necessity to include natural and human forces.

In this jurisdiction (and most others), murder is divided into two degrees:

  • First-degree murder – a killing committed with (1) the intent to kill—the purpose or knowledge that death will result—and (2) premeditation—when the defendant plans or reflects on the killing beforehand
  • Second-degree murder – all other common law murder—ie, an unlawful killing with malice aforethought

Here, the man intentionally shot and killed a rival gang member to save his own life. And since the man had reflected on the consequences of the killing the day before, his actions were premeditated. Therefore, the man will be convicted of the more serious offense of first-degree murder—unless he has a viable defense (Choice B).

The man's decision to kill the rival gang member because of the death threat he received from his own gang raises two possible defenses:

  • Duress – excuses criminal conduct when a human threat caused the defendant to reasonably believe that committing the crime was necessary to prevent imminent serious bodily harm or death
  • Necessity – justifies criminal conduct when a natural or human threat caused the defendant to reasonably believe that committing the crime was necessary to prevent a greater harm

But neither defense is available when the defendant is charged with murder (Choices C & D). Therefore, the jury should render a verdict finding the man guilty of first-degree murder.

The jury should render a verdict finding the man guilty of first-degree murder.

📌 Educational Objective

In most jurisdictions, an intentional and premeditated killing is categorized as first-degree murder. And neither duress (human threat) nor necessity (natural or human threat) is ever a defense to murder.

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被威胁去杀人时，duress（胁迫） 和 necessity（必要性） 都不能拿来挡 murder（谋杀），所以关键还是看有没有 intent to kill（杀人故意） 和 premeditation（预谋）。

三秒认题路径：

被逼杀人 → 先看谋杀 → 再看预谋 → 特权不救 → 选一级

核心法律规则

First-degree murder（一级谋杀） 的考场意思：杀人时有 intent to kill（杀人故意），而且事先已经想过、计划过，就是一级谋杀。Second-degree murder（二级谋杀） 只是其他普通法谋杀，也就是有恶意，但没有一级谋杀那种完整预谋。

Duress（胁迫） 的考场意思：它通常只救“非谋杀”的犯罪，而且前提是人身威胁逼你立刻下手。Necessity（必要性） 的考场意思：它也是一般抗辩，但这里同样不能用来抗 murder（谋杀）。

所以这题只剩一件事：他是“被逼”没错，但他还是主动开枪杀人，而且是前一天就已经反复想过，符合一级谋杀。

核心判例： Mohawk Industries v. Carpenter 不适用本题；本题真正锁定的是普通法下“胁迫和必要性都不是谋杀抗辩”的规则。

思维导图

先问：这是不是一级谋杀的认定题？
是 先看有没有 intent to kill（杀人故意）。
有 题干说他“开枪杀死”对方，故意成立。
再看 有没有 premeditation（预谋）。
有 他是“第二天”才动手，说明已经反复想过。
最后卡死 他说是为了保命，也只是想找抗辩。
但 duress（胁迫） 和 necessity（必要性） 都不能挡 murder（谋杀）。
结论 仍然是 Guilty of first-degree murder。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他是被帮派威胁才杀人，听起来像“不得已”，应该免罪。

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同理，帮派威胁很吓人，但它不把谋杀变成可用胁迫抗辩的案件；题干最致命的还是他提前一天就想过，直接把一级谋杀坐实了。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 第二天才开枪 说明已经预谋；而且他是故意杀人，符合一级谋杀。duress（胁迫） 和 necessity（必要性） 都不能把这题拉回无罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 低一级错判

✕ B: 把“有威胁”直接当成只能判二级，漏掉了 premeditation。

❌ 法律适用 | 胁迫套错题

✕ C: 想用 duress 直接洗掉谋杀，但这类抗辩本来就不能挡杀人。

❌ 事实误判 | 必要性偷换

✕ D: 把 necessity 当成“为了活命就无罪”，其实它也救不了谋杀。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定杀人等级，再看抗辩能不能进门；遇到谋杀，先别急着把胁迫和必要性当免死金牌。

考场速记

记住一句：intent + premeditation（故意 + 预谋） 就盯一级谋杀；遇到 duress（胁迫） 或 necessity（必要性），先想它们通常救不了 murder（谋杀）。

顺手背一个分辨法：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是上诉题口诀，不是这题的结论；本题只要抓住“预谋杀人 + 抗辩不通”，答案就落在一级谋杀。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man allowed his friend to borrow a debit card to buy a computer. When the friend refused to return the card during a later conversation in a bar, the man pointed a handgun at the friend, held his finger on the trigger, and said, "Give it back!" A bystander screamed and threw a beer bottle at the man. The bottle struck the man's hand and caused the gun to discharge, killing the friend instantly.
The man was convicted of murder in a jurisdiction that follows the common law of homicide. On appeal, he argues that the evidence, which essentially set out the facts above, was insufficient to support a verdict of murder.
Should the man's conviction be reversed?

choices.A: No, because the evidence was sufficient to support a verdict of depraved-heart murder.
choices.B: No, because the evidence was sufficient to support a verdict of felony murder.
choices.C: Yes, because the evidence showed that the man did not intentionally pull the trigger.
choices.D: Yes, because the evidence showed that the man's intent was not to kill the friend, but to take property from him under a claim of right.

questions.explanation:
A conviction should be reversed when the evidence presented at trial was insufficient to support a guilty verdict—ie, no reasonable fact finder could find proof of every element of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt. Common law murder requires proof of two elements: (1) the defendant unlawfully killed another (2) while acting with malice aforethought—ie:

  • intent to kill – purpose or knowledge that one's actions will cause death
  • intent to cause serious bodily injury – purpose or knowledge that one's actions will cause serious bodily injury
  • depraved-heart murder – reckless disregard for a high risk to human life or serious bodily injury
  • or
  • felony murder – intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony.

Here, the friend was accidentally killed when a bystander's beer bottle hit the man's hand and caused his gun to discharge (unlawful killing) (Choice C). Since the man had held his finger on the trigger while his gun was pointed at the friend, the man acted with reckless disregard for the high risk that his gun could discharge (malice aforethought). Therefore, the evidence is sufficient to support a verdict of depraved-heart murder, and the man's conviction should be affirmed (not reversed).

(Choice B) Felony murder is the unintentional killing of another during the commission, or attempted commission, of an inherently dangerous felony like robbery—ie, the trespassory taking and carrying away of another's property by force or threat with the intent to permanently deprive the owner thereof. Here, the killing occurred while the man was trying to recover his own debit card—not during an inherently dangerous felony.

(Choice D) An assertion that the defendant took property under a claim of right (ie, a claim of greater ownership) is a defense to theft crimes (eg, larceny, robbery)—not murder. And though the man did not intend to kill, the evidence supports a murder conviction since he recklessly pointed a loaded handgun at the friend.

📌 Educational Objective

A common law murder requires proof that the defendant unlawfully killed another person with malice aforethought, such as reckless indifference to human life (depraved-heart murder)—eg, pointing a loaded gun at another.
questions.zh-question:
一名男子允许其朋友借用一张借记卡购买电脑。后来在酒吧交谈时，朋友拒绝归还该卡，该男子遂用手枪指着朋友，手指放在扳机上，说道：“还给我！”一名旁观者尖叫起来，并向该男子扔了一个啤酒瓶。啤酒瓶击中了男子的手，导致枪支走火，当场打死了朋友。

该男子的定罪应被推翻吗？

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Types of homicide

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：common law murder 里的 恶性鲁莽杀人（depraved-heart murder），看被告有没有对高风险生命危险表现出极端轻率，而不是只盯着他有没有亲手扣扳机。

三秒认题路径：

共同法谋杀 → 恶性鲁莽 → 高风险开枪 → 不必亲扣扳机 → 选 A

核心法律规则

common law murder（共同法谋杀）要先有“非法杀人”，再有 malice aforethought（预谋恶意，考场意思：不是一时失手，而是带着杀意或极端危险心态）。

depraved-heart murder（恶性鲁莽杀人，考场意思：明知道自己在制造很高的致死风险，还照样干）就是 malice aforethought 的一种。

所以本题只要题干事实够到“拿着上膛枪、手指压在扳机上、对着人威胁”，即使最后是被旁人丢瓶子触发走火，仍然能支持 murder。

核心判例：本题对应的规则就是 depraved-heart 路径：不用证明他想杀死对方，只要证明他对高风险生命危险漠视到极点即可。

思维导图

先问：这是 murder conviction 的上诉，证据够不够？
1. 是否有 unlawful killing（非法杀人）？
有：枪支因争执而走火，友人当场死亡
2. 是否有 malice aforethought（预谋恶意）？
有：把上膛手枪对着人，手指一直压在扳机上
3. 走哪条 malice 路径？
恶性鲁莽（depraved-heart）
卡死点：不要求“亲手扣扳机”
4. 结论
证据足够 → 维持定罪 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他不是自己主动把扳机扣下去，所以最多算失手，不能算 murder。

但考试真正问的是：他当时是否已经对“拿枪对人、手指压扳机”这种高风险行为表现出恶性鲁莽。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 本题同理，重点不是“谁最后碰到扳机”，而是“谁先把人命风险推到极高”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 持枪指向朋友且手指压在扳机上，已经够成对生命的极端漠视；即便是旁人打中手臂才走火，仍足以支持 depraved-heart murder。

❌ 法律适用 | 重罪前提误判

✕ B: 把 felony murder 硬套进来；这里不是在实施本身危险的重罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 扣扳机偷换

✕ C: 只盯着没亲扣 trigger，忽略了他早就把致死风险推上去了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 盗窃抗辩误套

✕ D: 把 claim of right 当成谋杀抗辩；这只管盗窃类，不管杀人定性。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 common law murder 的 malice，再看题干有没有“对高风险生命危险的恶性鲁莽”。

考场速记

记住：depraved-heart murder 不是“想杀人”才算，而是“明知危险还照做”。看到 loaded gun 对人、手指压扳机、还继续威胁，先想到恶性鲁莽，通常就是谋杀成立。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man became angry after he was unexpectedly laid off from his longtime job as a factory worker. The next day, he returned to the factory floor and indiscriminately fired shotgun rounds into the air. The man later testified, without contradiction, that he had not intended to kill anyone but had simply sought to exact revenge on the factory's owners by shutting down operations for the day. Unfortunately, one of the bullets ricocheted off the wall and killed the man's best friend.
The crimes below are listed in descending order of seriousness.
On these facts, what is the most serious offense of which the man properly could be convicted?

choices.A: Murder.
choices.B: Voluntary manslaughter.
choices.C: Involuntary manslaughter.
choices.D: Assault.

questions.explanation:
Homicide
Common law Modern approach
Murder Unlawful killing committed with malice aforethought:
  • Intent to kill
  • Intent to cause serious bodily harm
  • Depraved-heart murder
  • Felony murder
 First-degree: murder committed with:
  • premeditation & deliberation
  • heinous acts (eg, bombing, torture)
  • enumerated felony murder
Second-degree: any murder that is not first-degree murder
Voluntary
manslaughter		 Intentional killing mitigated by either:
  • adequate provocation (ie, heat of passion)
  • other mitigating factors (eg, imperfect self-defense)
Involuntary
manslaughter		 Unintentional killing either:
  • caused by criminal negligence (or recklessness under MPC)
  • occurs during commission of criminal act (eg, misdemeanor manslaughter)
MPC = Model Penal Code.

Murder is the unlawful killing of another with malice aforethought. Four types of mental states satisfy the malice aforethought requirement:

  • Intent to kill – the purpose or knowledge that one's conduct will cause the victim's death
  • Intent to cause serious bodily injury – the purpose or knowledge that one's conduct will cause serious bodily injury or a significant risk of death
  • Depraved-heart murder – reckless indifference to an obvious or high risk to human life
  • Felony murder – intent to commit an inherently dangerous felony

Here, the best friend was killed when the man's bullet ricocheted off a factory wall. Although the man did not intend to kill his best friend, he did act with reckless indifference to human life by indiscriminately firing shotgun rounds into the air inside the factory (depraved-heart murder). Therefore, the man properly could be convicted of murder.

(Choice B) Voluntary manslaughter is an intentional killing of another prompted by adequate provocation (or imperfect self-defense) and committed before a reasonable cooling-off period has elapsed. Here, the man could not be convicted of voluntary manslaughter since (1) he did not intend to kill his best friend, (2) an unexpected layoff is not adequate provocation, and (3) the murder occurred a day later—after he had cooled off.

(Choice C) Involuntary manslaughter is an unintentional killing of another (1) during the commission of an unlawful act or (2) with criminal negligence. Although the man could be convicted of involuntary manslaughter (since he killed the best friend while unreasonably firing a shotgun in the factory), he could also be convicted of the more serious crime of murder.

(Choice D) Assault is an attempted battery or the intentional infliction of reasonable apprehension of imminent bodily harm. Here, the man could be convicted of assault since he intended to shut down factory operations for the day by causing apprehension of imminent bodily harm with his shotgun. But murder is a more serious offense.

📌 Educational Objective

Murder is an unlawful killing committed intentionally (ie, intent to kill or inflict serious bodily injury), during the commission or attempted commission of an inherently dangerous felony (ie, felony murder), or with reckless disregard for human life (ie, depraved-heart murder).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Definition

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：恶意预谋杀人（malice aforethought）里，轻率漠视人命（depraved-heart murder）足够把“没想杀这个人”也拉进 murder。

三秒认题路径：

没想杀人 → 乱喷霰弹枪 → 高度危险 → 漠视人命 → 选 Murder

核心法律规则

谋杀（murder）要求 恶意预谋（malice aforethought），考场上最常见的四条路是：意图杀人（intent to kill）、意图造成重伤（intent to cause serious bodily harm）、轻率漠视人命（depraved-heart murder）、重罪谋杀（felony murder）。轻率漠视人命 的考场意思：明知道会把人命推到高风险里，还硬做。
本题里，他在工厂里随意朝空中打霰弹枪，虽然嘴上说不是为了杀朋友，但这种行为本身就够 reckless indifference，所以仍可定 murder。
自愿过失杀人（voluntary manslaughter） 要的是“本来是故意杀人，但被 adequate provocation 降档”；这里既没有合格挑衅，也已经过了一天，冷静期早过去了。
非自愿过失杀人（involuntary manslaughter） 只适合不故意的杀人，常见于 criminal negligence；它比 murder 轻，所以就算沾得上，也不是最严重罪名。

核心判例： 本题对应的考点逻辑就是 depraved-heart murder：对明显或高度人命风险的冷漠下注，足以锁定谋杀。

思维导图

先看：有没有 malice aforethought？
有：他不是误伤，而是 在工厂里乱射霰弹枪，把人命风险直接抬高。
再问：有没有 intent to kill？
没有。口头说法只是不想杀“朋友”，不是杀人故意。
再问：有没有 depraved-heart murder？
有。对工厂内人的生命危险显而易见，他仍然无差别开枪。
结果：即使最后是 ricochet 误中朋友，结论仍是 Murder。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他没有“想杀朋友”，那就只能算轻一点的 manslaughter。

但考试真正问的是：他做事时有没有把人命故意丢进高风险里；这里看的是 reckless indifference，不是最后死的是不是“原本想杀的人”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个坑是把“想让工厂停工”误读成无害动机；动机不洗白 depraved-heart，危险行为本身才是关键。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 indiscriminately fired shotgun rounds，属于对人命的高度漠视；即使没想杀朋友，也已满足 depraved-heart murder。

❌ 概念混淆 | 挑衅误认

✕ B: 把 unexpectedly laid off 当成合格挑衅，且他早就冷静下来了。

❌ 法律适用 | 轻罪降档误套

✕ C: 只盯着“没想杀”，忽略了这种 recklessly 开枪已经升到谋杀。

❌ 事实误判 | 伤害类型偷换

✕ D: 把“想停工”说成只是吓唬人，但题干已经发生了致命结果。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓杀人心态，再看危险程度；只要是无差别高危射击，先往 murder 想。

考场速记

记住：malice aforethought 不只等于“想杀人”，还包括“明知危险仍硬上”。

口诀：故意杀、重伤杀、重罪杀、漠视杀，四路里只要撞上一条，先按 murder 处理。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A homeowner set fire to his residence to collect on his fire insurance policy. Before setting the fire, the homeowner, realizing that the fire would create a great risk that someone could die, carefully checked the residence to ensure that no one was inside. Later, a firefighter who was called to put out the fire was killed when a wall of the residence collapsed due to the fire. The applicable jurisdiction adheres to the common law regarding the crimes of murder and arson.
Could the homeowner be found guilty of murder?

choices.A: No, because the homeowner did not intend for anyone to die as a result of the fire.
choices.B: No, because the homeowner is not guilty of arson.
choices.C: Yes, because the homeowner acted with premeditation when setting the fire.
choices.D: Yes, because the homeowner realized the danger that the fire represented to human life.

questions.explanation:
Depraved-heart murder (reckless indifference to human life)

To find a defendant guilty of common-law murder, the evidence must show that the defendant unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—i.e., the defendant:

  • intended to kill – acted with the purpose or knowledge that his actions would cause a death
  • intended to cause serious bodily injury – acted with the purpose or knowledge that his actions would cause significant but nonfatal injury
  • acted with reckless indifference to an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of serious bodily harm or death (i.e., depraved-heart murder) or
  • intended to commit an inherently dangerous felony (i.e., felony-murder rule).

Here, the homeowner intentionally set fire to his residence, and a firefighter was killed while putting out the fire. The homeowner had not intended for anyone to die as a result of the fire because he checked the residence to ensure that no one was inside before setting the fire. However, this demonstrates that the homeowner realized the danger that the fire represented to human life (reckless indifference), satisfying the intent requirement for depraved-heart murder (Choice D). Therefore, the homeowner could be found guilty of murder.

(Choice B) The homeowner is not guilty of arson for setting fire to his home because common-law arson is the malicious burning of another's dwelling. As a result, the felony-murder doctrine is inapplicable. But the homeowner acted with a depraved heart by setting fire to his home, satisfying the intent requirement for murder.

(Choice C) Premeditation requires that the defendant fully form the specific intent to kill before committing the act. While the homeowner did not have the intent to kill, he did act with reckless indifference to an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of serious bodily harm or death. This satisfies the requisite intent for murder.

📌 Educational Objective

For common-law murder, the defendant must have unlawfully killed another with malice aforethought—e.g., acted with reckless indifference to an obvious or unjustifiably high risk of serious bodily harm or death (i.e., depraved-heart murder).

MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Homicide - Intended killings

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告虽然没想杀人，但明知纵火会对人命造成极高危险，还照做了，这就是 reckless indifference 支撑的 depraved-heart murder。

三秒认题路径：

纵火 → 高风险 → 查无人 → 仍放火 → 德心谋杀

核心法律规则

只看本题要用的规则

common-law murder 考场意思：只要有 malice aforethought，就可能成立 murder，不一定非要“想杀人”。

depraved-heart murder 考场意思：被告对“明显而不合理的致死或重伤高风险”表现出 reckless indifference，就够了。

这题里，屋主先确认屋内没人，说明他不是冲着“当场杀人”去的；但他明知火会威胁人命还点火，所以满足 murder 的恶意要件。

核心判例： 无需具体判例名也能定案：本题直接落在 depraved-heart murder，不是 premeditation。

思维导图

先问：有没有 malice aforethought？
不是只是说“我没想杀人” → 不够，继续看有没有 reckless indifference
是屋主知道纵火会把人命放进高风险里
关键卡点：他查屋内没人，打掉的是“故意杀人”，打不掉的是“明知高危还去做”
结论：depraved-heart murder 成立 → 选 D
别被“没有预谋”带偏：premeditation 只管故意杀人，不管这种高危鲁莽杀人。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他先检查没人，说明他没有杀人故意，所以不能算 murder。

questions.question:
A wife decided to kill her husband because she was tired of his infidelity. She managed to obtain some cyanide, a deadly poison. One evening, she poured wine laced with the cyanide into a glass, handed it to her husband, and proposed a loving toast. The husband was so pleased with the toast that he set the glass of wine down on a table, grabbed his wife, and kissed her passionately. After the kiss, the wife changed her mind about killing the husband. She hid the glass of wine behind a lamp on the table, planning to leave it for the maid to clean up. The husband did not drink the wine.
The maid found the glass of wine while cleaning the next day. Rather than throw the wine away, the maid drank it. Shortly thereafter, she fell into a coma and died from cyanide poisoning.
In a common law jurisdiction, of what crime(s), if any, could the wife be found guilty?

choices.A: Attempted murder of the husband and murder or manslaughter of the maid.
choices.B: Only attempted murder of the husband.
choices.C: Only murder or manslaughter of the maid.
choices.D: No crime.
